relevance: A framework for measuring what context actually costs coding agents.

media.description: Abstract excerpt of a paper on context policies for coding agents, measuring executed prefill with prefix caching; on 450 SWE-rebench V2 localization cases, eager preloading of retrieved blocks cuts model calls 35.7% and a GPU-energy proxy 33.2% versus on-demand grep.
media.ocr_text: Coding agents resend a growing context on every model call, and context policies are usually judged by the prompt tokens they save. Executed work also depends on call count and prefix reuse: a caching runtime prefills only the tokens after the longest cached prefix. A shorter prompt can therefore cost more if it rewrites cached history. Our quality-gated protocol splits executed prefill into logical prompt minus reused prefix and measures KV residency, time, and energy. On 450 localization cases derived from SWE-rebench V2, preloading ten retrieved blocks (Eager) and adding anchored history compaction (Compact) both pass a five-point non-inferiority gate. In a separate 900-cell study, Eager cuts model calls by 35.7% and the GPU-energy proxy by 33.2% against on-demand search (Grep); Compact saves nothing further.
